$comment: OpenClaw/MCP tool manifest for the Nara-on-NemoClaw agent bundle (β groundwork; 4-tool slice: submit_loop_iteration + poll_run added 2026-06-10 to close the 15s MCP client-timeout gap). STATIC MIRROR of orchestrator/tool_plane.py's GET /tools — keep the two in lockstep (tests/test_tool_plane.py::test_manifest_matches_the_agent_bundle_tool_name guards all four names). The agent runs INSIDE nara-sandbox and reaches this HOST endpoint through the proven egress alias host.openshell.internal:8077 (egress preset nara-host-tool-plane is applied LIVE, policy revision 15). See docs/nemoclaw_agent_run_runbook.md.
$mirror_note: L1 owns the host-side plane endpoint POST /tools/run_loop_iteration + the schema/iteration_record.schema.json seed.source enum 'nemoclaw_agent'. This manifest is the agent-side mirror of L1's contract; until the integrator lands L1's plane edit, the live plane serves only get_apparatus_state and this run_loop_iteration entry is ahead of the plane (a known, intended transient — the mirror is truthful once L1 lands).

transport.$comment: base_url is the PROVEN host alias. The sandbox reaches the host via OpenShell's host alias host.openshell.internal (NOT the host hostname spark-7eeb, NOT a raw IP — those 403 under the egress/SSRF guard). Verified end-to-end 2026-06-09: a sandbox POST get_apparatus_state at this base_url returned the live snapshot. Port 8077 = the tool plane's --port.

tools.name: get_apparatus_state
tools.description: Return a compact, read-only snapshot of the a_bgt_rsi research apparatus (in-flight run, recent loop findings, open threads, gaps, surfaced/pending findings, experiments, and one morning-loop topic suggestion). Pure read; mutates nothing.

tools.name: run_loop_iteration
tools.description: Run exactly ONE bounded LOOP_V0 iteration on a research topic, host-side: Nara chains hypothesize -> retrieve_literature -> novelty_classify -> critic_loop_v0 -> journal_writer and returns the verdict. The topic is validated SERVER-SIDE (an off-domain or thin-evidence topic trips the host's low-evidence gate — a correct signal, not a failure). This is the ONE write-capable tool in the bundle: it triggers a single iteration and nothing else (no spawn, no commit, no trade). One-at-a-time is enforced host-side. For MCP clients prefer submit_loop_iteration + poll_run (this call blocks ~90s and may exceed client timeouts).

invocation.$comment: Body: {"topic": "<thesis sentence>"}. Response envelope (L1 contract): {"tool": "run_loop_iteration", "ok": true|false, "result": {"iteration_id", "novelty_class", "critic_verdict", "low_confidence", ...}}. The iteration record is stamped seed.source="nemoclaw_agent". A server-side validation failure (off-domain / thin topic) returns ok:false with a reason — report it honestly, do NOT retry or rephrase to force a pass.

tools.name: submit_loop_iteration
tools.description: Submit ONE LOOP_V0 research iteration to run host-side and return IMMEDIATELY with a run_id ticket (the iteration itself takes ~1-3 minutes of host GPU compute). Same boundary as run_loop_iteration: server-side topic validation and one iteration at a time — a busy apparatus refuses, nothing is queued. Poll the ticket with poll_run. Prefer THIS over run_loop_iteration when calling over MCP (the synchronous call blocks ~90s and exceeds the client's 15s request timeout).

invocation.$comment: Body: {"topic": "<thesis sentence>"}. Response in milliseconds: {"tool": "submit_loop_iteration", "ok": true, "result": {"run_id": "mcpsub-...", "status": "running", "poll_with": "poll_run"}}. A busy apparatus returns ok:false error "iteration_in_flight" naming the blocking run — report it honestly, do NOT retry in a loop. Exactly one iteration per submit; nothing is queued.

tools.name: poll_run
tools.description: Poll a run_id ticket returned by submit_loop_iteration. While running, returns honest reads of the run registry entry and the host's live active-iteration step board; once terminal, the finished verdict envelope (iteration_id, novelty_class, critic_verdict, low_confidence, journal path) or the failure. Pure read, except that a ticket whose server process died is reconciled to failed/server_restart_mid_run. Only tickets from submit_loop_iteration are pollable (anything else: unknown_run_id).

invocation.$comment: Body: {"run_id": "mcpsub-..."}. Running: {"ok": true, "result": {"status": "running", "registry": {...}, "heartbeat_age_s": n, "stale": bool, "active_iteration": {"iteration_id", "current_step", "latest_narration", "steps": [...], "updated_at"}}} — active_iteration.updated_at is the live progress signal; `stale` is informational. Finished: result.result carries the same verdict fields run_loop_iteration returns. Failed: {"status": "failed", "error": ...} with ok:true (the poll succeeded — report the run failure honestly). Poll every ~15-30s until terminal; do not spin.
